title: clearance.evidence/v1
description: One Clearance evidence record (docs/evidence.md). Flat: every field is a top-level key, grouped by x-clearance-group into Identities, Source, Target, Provenance, Decision, Outcome, Coverage, Assurance, Intent and Integrity, and tagged verified or claimed by the record's own lists. Fields not listed here are allowed and are claimed unless the writer verified them. The chain rule is the same for every version. Revision 4 (O-1) is clearance.evidence/v1.1: additive, so the same file describes v1 and v1.1. A record says v1.1 only when it is an observation kind (observation, assessment, resolution, observation.health, observation.audit-gap) or its coverage is break-glass or attempted-refused; every other record is still written as v1.

schema.description: The record shape it was written in. Writers emit clearance.evidence/v1, or clearance.evidence/v1.1 for a record that uses an observation kind or the coverage states break-glass and attempted-refused; v0-draft appears only on rows written before the freeze (seq 0-611 on hangar-dev), served projected.

seq.description: Position in the chain, from 0, no gaps.

ts.description: When the writer recorded it, UTC, second precision.

prev_hash.description: hash of record seq-1; 64 zeros for seq 0.

hash.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8) of the stored record without hash.

verified.description: The fields the writer established itself, sorted.

claimed.description: The fields something else asserted, sorted. verified + claimed name every field outside the envelope.

boundary.description: Which boundary wrote it: the runtime gateway (a call) or the deployment gate (a change).

conformance.description: The conformance suite the provider passed and when (clearance-conformance/v1@YYYY-MM-DD), from its registration (CLEARANCE_PROVIDERS conformance).

provider.description: The registered provider that wrote the record. Set by the writer from its registration, never by the event. The Python gateway is autopilot-gateway.

subject.description: What the record is about, in in-toto subject style: kind and digests keyed by algorithm (sha256, gitCommit). Null when the record has no subject (an unregistered deployment).

app.description: The application the record acts on, for correlation and ownership.

task_id.description: The task tree the record belongs to; correlates runtime and deployment records.

parent.description: The parent session in a run tree.

principal.description: The authenticated caller: a workload, a person (user:<login>), an App installation (app:<id>), a pin (pin:<ns>/<xr>) or policy.

initiator.description: The initiating human, by IdP subject and issuer. Optional.

model_version.description: Optional (revision 3, AP-C1): on a run's records (session.open, run.launch, run.finish, run.delete), the pinned model version the run runs on (its definition's model through the provider's route); on a model.call outcome, the model that answered, as its provider named it. Claimed.

tool.description: The operation: a tool name (repo.pr.open), or the record's event type (session.open, model.call, deploy.request, provenance.verify).

args_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the call's arguments. Arguments are never stored.

change.description: The gate's view of a change (deployment records): id, app, env, cluster, head, tree, tier, state, objects.

source.description: Optional: repository, revision and image digests behind the subject.

target.description: What the call is aimed at: an environment tier, a model, a repo#pr, a pin, a request id.

destination.description: Optional: cluster, environment and Argo application a change lands in.

provenance.description: Optional: provenance confidence and the signals behind it, each tagged.

rule.description: The rule that decided (a deny rule id, or the rule an allow noted).

rules.description: Optional: every rule that fired, in order.

reason.description: Optional: the plain-language reason, apart from the result.

policy.description: Optional: the policy that decided. A runtime decision (R-5): ref names the core and each policy bundle with its version, version is their digest, engine is cel-go. A deployment decision (C-8): ref is clearance.yaml@<commit> (or clearance.yaml@sha256:<digest>, or baseline), version the gate baseline plus the clearance.yaml digest, engine the admission engine and version the verifier ran offline (kyverno/1.19.0, or none), verdict its result (pass, warn, fail, skipped, error, or not-evaluated) and bundle the admission rule set it ran (<repo>//<path>@<commit>).

approvals.description: Optional: approver subjects with issuer, channel and time.

preflight.description: Optional (revision 3, AP-C1): on a run's records, the Preflight result of the run's definition: pass or fail once A-6 scores it, not-run until then. Claimed.

result.description: The call's result line, or the reason of a deny (v0 semantics, kept).

effect.description: The receipt of a write the writer made itself (repo, pr).

refusal.description: Optional (revision 2): on an outcome, a refusal the provider's handler made after the core allowed the call (a rule the core cannot see), with its rule id and message. Claimed; the record's decision and rule stay the decision's.

usage.description: Optional (revision 3, AP-C2): on a model.call outcome, the call's token usage as the provider's model proxy metered it (the provider's four kinds, every one present) and charged_tokens, the call's weighted charge (the session's model_tokens budget counts it up to its limit; a call that overruns it trips the breaker and the record keeps the whole charge). clearance-api's counts by=cost sums it per task, session, agent or principal. Claimed.

cost.description: Optional (revision 3, AP-C2): on run.finish, the run's own summary: its sessions' model usage summed, its model and tool calls, how long it ran and its compute class. The counts sum the model.call outcomes for tokens, never this, so a run is not counted twice. Claimed.

outcome.description: Optional: deployment result, observed revision and digest, health, rollback.

exception.description: Revision 3 (C-6): on deploy.exception, what landed outside a clearance and how it was found: out-of-band (objects), drift (addresses or objects), untraced-apply (actor), digest-mismatch (expected, observed; the record names the change). Claimed; the core sets coverage from the kind. Revision 4 (O-1): attempted-refused (actor, detail: refused, nothing landed; coverage attempted-refused) and monitoring-protection (actor, detail: an operation on the controls that watch the environment, tier 3 whether or not it succeeded).

coverage.description: How the event was observed: authorized-and-verified, observed-not-attributed, out-of-band-detected, coverage-unavailable, and from v1.1 break-glass (inside a declared break-glass window) and attempted-refused (an operation something tried and a control refused) (an enum in v1; v0-draft rows carry what they were written with).

outage.description: Revision 3 (C-6): on deploy.degraded, the window the provider could not reach the core (RFC 3339). Claimed.

outage_policy.description: Revision 3 (C-6): on deploy.degraded, added and verified by the core: the outage policy's action for the change (its registered outage, the baseline for the claimed tier, or hold for an unknown tier) and whether the provider's decision conformed.

breakglass.description: Revision 3 (C-6), verified: on breakglass.open and breakglass.close the window {id, cluster, env, app, ...}; on a deploy.exception or deploy.degraded inside an open window, the window's id.

window.description: Revision 3 (C-6): on breakglass.close, when the window was open. Verified.

changes.description: Revision 3 (C-6): on breakglass.close, the records the store holds about the window's environment written while it was open (at most 200; reported is the full count, truncated says when the list or the scan was cut). Verified.

reported.description: Revision 3 (C-6): on breakglass.close, how many records the window had. Verified.

truncated.description: Revision 3 (C-6): on breakglass.close, whether changes was cut. Verified.

limitations.description: Revision 3 (C-6): on breakglass.close, what the record store cannot know about the window. Verified.

assurance.description: Kept beside the record, never hashed: whether its hash is under a witnessed checkpoint. Added by a reader (clearance-api).

intent.description: Why, as stated by the agent or the change: redacted (the default) keeps only the SHA-256 of the text; full keeps the text, where the deployment opts in.

projected.description: Added by a reader: the fields it derived for a v0-draft row (provider, subject). They are not covered by hash; drop them, assurance and projected before re-hashing.

scope.description: Revision 4 (O-1): on the observation kinds, the account, cluster or workspace the record speaks for. Claimed.

resource.description: Revision 4 (O-1): on an observation, what was acted on. A Secret is observed at Metadata only: its observation names it and carries no state_change and no body.

subject.description: The verified subject the source established.

chain.description: Who assumed whom, first to last.

client.description: Self-reported by the actor (a user agent, a tool name): never a basis for attribution.

actor.description: Revision 4 (O-1): on an observation, who did it, split into the verified subject, the chain of identities it came through, the issuer, the self-reported client and attributes.

action.description: Revision 4 (O-1): on an observation, what was done: the verb, the API called, whether it succeeded and, if refused, why. protects_monitoring marks an operation on the controls that watch the environment (configuration can mark them too, CLEARANCE_MONITORING_PROTECTION_OPS).

state_change.description: Revision 4 (O-1): on an observation, the resource's state before and after, where a state service has it. Never present on a Secret.

correlation.description: Revision 4 (O-1): on an observation, the clearance, plan, task, run and operation it correlates with, as the source reported them. Claimed.

sourceVerified.description: The delivered log files were verified unaltered (for example a trail's digest chain).

completenessClaimed.description: The provider claims the feed delivered everything for the period; supported only if the feed's health record says so.

integrity.description: Revision 4 (O-1): on an observation, source integrity (sourceVerified) split from completeness (completenessClaimed). Whether the health record supports the completeness claim is the core's own conclusion, completeness_supported.

completeness_supported.description: Revision 4 (O-1): on an observation, added and verified by the core: the scope and source's latest health record was healthy and not stale when the observation arrived.

times.description: Revision 4 (O-1): on an observation, when the action was requested, observed and delivered to the provider (RFC 3339). ts is when the core recorded it.

health.description: Revision 4 (O-1): on observation.health, a feed's state per scope and source and the checks that produced it. healthy only when every check passed. A health record older than twice interval_seconds (default 900) is stale, and a stale feed is blind.

about.description: Revision 4 (O-1): on an assessment or a resolution, the record it is about (an observation; for a resolution also an assessment); on a health record the core derived, the observation that flipped it. The core checks the record exists and is in the same scope.

rule_set.description: Revision 4 (O-1): on an assessment, the version of the rule set that decided its coverage.

attribution.description: Revision 4 (O-1): on an assessment, the attribution signal that decided its coverage (for example a grant match, a break-glass window, the absence of any grant).

resolution.description: Revision 4 (O-1): on a resolution, how an observed change ended. A reverted resolution carries its cause; no other state does.

gap.description: Revision 4 (O-1): on observation.audit-gap, written by the core when a scope and source's feed went from healthy (or unseen) to degraded or blind: the state, why and the health record that said so. Verified.
